>celerity deck. The gangrel deck is based on the following combat combo:

You have a problem. As far as I can tell, there's no _easy_ way to get
around this. You could toss in a bunch of Sideslips to use at superior,
but that only prevents one damage. Perhaps when added with flak jackets
or Guardian Angels...? Otherwise, I'm not sure you're going to get very
far against a Gangrel deck with a Brujah cel/pot deck. You could include
some Majesties (assuming you have an adequate amount of presence too...).
However, your main problem (aside from sucking agg...) is, I'm willing to
bet, the Gangrel deck taking everything you can dish out with its
Fortitude. You can always pile on more Fists of Death or Torn Signposts
or Death of My Conscience, but then again, Skin of Steel is pretty common...
Pretty much the only way to get around the Scorpion Sting combo is either
Fortitude (or alternate damage prevention) of your own, or Strike: Combat
Ends, as far as I'm aware. I suppose there are also some cards in Sabbat
that turn agg to normal, but I believe they're farily few & far between.

>Drawing out the beast +
>scorpian sting (superior) +
>bone spur or wolf claws

>result is my brujah can't maneuver or dodge in combat so they take two
>aggravated damage.

>Please help

My recommendation would be to build another deck. Not specifically
designed to kill the Gangrel deck, because that's boring. But as a
suggestion, a thaumaturgy/fortitude deck (with some intercept) can be
utter death to Gangrel decks, or something simpler with damage
prevention. Potence/Fortitude if you want something outlandish, or a
straight Ventrue Dom/For/Pre deck would work nice...throw some votes in
for fun. Anoter option would be a Brujah Presence/Potence (and/or Celerity)
deck. Toss in Rake, other small guys with votes, maybe Carthage Remembered
for fun...Burning Wrath, use Majesty when you're worried, otherwise,
Immortal Grapple and pound your opponent. But Flak jackets are probably
a plus.

--Xian

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Rob LeGood wrote:
"One word: Rotschreck. Throw 5 or so in when you know you're going
against an agg. deck. People get surprisingly paranoid over this wonderful
little card."

Well, sure, but then you open up the horible world of "Side Boarding" and
specific deck killers. Once you start down that road, it won't be long
before everone starts putting in 6 Brujah Frenzies to defeat that Brujah
deck or 10 Nosferatu Putrescence just because they know some guy is
playing who always plays Nosferatu. Your group may like this sort of
play, but the world of "Trumping Trumps" is generally considered a bad
idea (and not needed in Jyhad).

A better way to deal with the Brujah/Gangrel problem is to try to fix the
deck proper to deal with these problems, rather than planning on putting
in "Screw the Gangrel" cards when you know you are playing the Gangrel
(this isn't Magic, ya know :-).

First, look at the problem: The Brujah can't really prevent damage
effectively, and the Gangrel make it impossible for you to Dodge. My
first answer would be "Then don't fight the Gangrel". If you know you
can't beat them, don't try. The best card to put in your deck for this
reason is the Sabbat card Staredown. While at first glance, Staredown
appears completely inferior to Majesty, in a Brujah combat deck, it is
perfect, as you can always use it to Dodge and then Additional Strike if
you don't need the S:CE. Replace all of your Sideslips/Acrobatics with
Staredown, and S:CE (which the Gangrel can only deal with by having Dog
Packs, which are expensive and fragile) when you get in a fight you can't
win.

When that fails, make a new deck. Every possible deck design can be
beaten senseless by another one (a S+B deck vs a heavy Wake/Deflections
deck, Brujah combat vs a Gangrel Scorpion Sting deck, a Gangrel Deck vs a
heavy S:CE deck, a Potence Immortal Grapple deck vs a deck full of Skin of
Steel, ect...). By making lots of new decks all the time, no one in your
play group can capitalize upon the weakness of a particular deck that
someone plays every week.

This card works (officially) by being played on a vampire as that
vampire attempts to deal aggravated damage in combat.

> and why?

Because that's how the Rule Team has ruled/errataed it to work.

> It seems to me like card text and the rules team ruling are in complete
> disagreement, so I'm curious why you would pick one over the other.

You would pick the official version because it is official.
You could pick a house rule only if your group agrees to it.

BTW (and not to say you're wrong for playing Rot the way it is
written - my group uses the same house rule), I think this line
of attack ("why use RT errata over printed text?") won't serve
well in the long run.

For instance, do you burn a vampire if his last blood is stolen?
(Official: "No" / Print: "Yes")

Another: Is playing the P/J card Blood Hunt directed or undirected?

--
L. Scott Johnson (vte...@regency.wizards.com)

Oh, I totally agree. In the case of this specific card, we banned it,
since people would attempt to play it and arguments about what the card
does would ensue. In my mind, if we were to play with the card, I would
be for the text version (i.e., the house rule), since it seems to make
more sense.

I guess I just want to know how pervasive Rotschreck is. When we banned
it, it seemed to me like this was the norm; people disagreed with the RT
ruling, and thus the card was made useless (in the sense that it _could_
not be used). I'm wondering now if maybe we should have chosen one side
of the fence or the other, instead of bulldozing the fence...

First off, the Brujah seldom can match the Gangrel in head-on
combat. So what if you can do 46 damage in a given round if I
can do one agg. damage and play skin of steel. However, there
are many other strategies which can kill the Gangrel. Weenie
pool gain/Hostile Takover is always an interesting strategy
against them, and the Tremere, used properly, can counter them
as well with Thoughts Betrayed massacre combos or, on a more
equitable level with first round anti-fortitude strikes (Blood
Fury or Theft of Vitae) to get the licks in, and fortitude for
yourself to avoid the agg damage. Stealth and bleed or vote
can usually give the Gangrel a hard time as well.

Dave Green
